items.title: Prostate cancer.

canonicalFacts.claim: Six systemic agents have been approved for castration-resistant prostate cancer treatment in the last decade.
PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy has reshaped treatment landscape for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with lutetium-177 PSMA-617 showing significant overall survival benefits.
Personalized therapeutics targeting genomic alterations in DNA repair pathways are now clinically validated for prostate cancer treatment.

redFlags: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw can occur with bisphosphonates, denosumab, and antiangiogenic agents used in cancer treatment
Vertebral fractures can occur after denosumab discontinuation, with increased risk of multiple vertebral fractures

excludedAgents.name: Ipatasertib
excludedAgents.reason: Phase 3 trial failed to show benefit when added to abiraterone and prednisolone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer

excludedAgents.name: Metformin
excludedAgents.reason: Phase III randomized trial showed no efficacy in delaying prostate cancer progression in men with low-risk disease on active surveillance

excludedAgents.name: Curcumin
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial found no anti-cancer activity in prostate cancer patients receiving intermittent androgen deprivation

excludedAgents.name: Ipilimumab
excludedAgents.reason: Phase 3 trial failed to show benefit versus placebo after radiotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that progressed after docetaxel

excludedAgents.name: Nanocurcumin
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized trial failed to show significant benefit in preventing radiation-induced proctitis in prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy
